params.body:
## What

Superseding deletes nothing in the pipeline: the old reading stays, marked `superseded`, and points at what replaced it. Two things were missing.

**When.** The date lived only in the lifecycle log, and only for the 85 twins folded today. Merges and refinements had none on the row.

**Where an old address should go.** The site does drop a superseded card, so since today's fold 85 public trend addresses answer 404, and so does `get_trend` in the agent door, which tells agents to cite a trend by its url. The site already has the rule for this in its own comment ("a 404 on what worked yesterday is the most expensive way to improve an address") and applies it to old ids.

## How

- `superseded_at` on `insights`, set wherever `superseded_by` is set: `consolidate` (a merge), `linkRefinement` (a refinement), `linkTwins` (a twin fold).
- A one-time migration (`superseded-at-2026-09-23`) dates the existing ones: from the lifecycle log's own `superseded` event where there is one, else from the birth of what replaced it (for a merge and a refinement that is the moment it took over), else `updated_at`.
- `listShowcaseInsights` gives each public card `absorbed`: the public ids that now resolve to it, with headline and date. Only public ids, because a draft that never had a page has no address to keep. It travels to the site through the trend projection unchanged, since the card spreads the showcase item.

The site side (an alias table, a 301 to the absorbing trend, and `get_trend` saying what happened) follows in its own PR on gentells-site.

## Tests

`test/twins.test.mjs` now also pins that a twin fold and a refinement set the date, and that the card that stays lists what it absorbed while an untouched card lists nothing.
params.title: A superseded reading says since when, and its card says what it absorbed
